````text
# #1800: Patch: every foreign key that a delete or a lookup walks has an index, and the schema check keeps it so
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
The game's database links rows together: a matchmaking ticket to its match, a logged move to the player who made it, a result to its winner. When a linked row is deleted, or the server looks rows up by such a link, the database must read the whole linking table unless that link has an index. Today 19 of the schema's 86 links have none. Some of them are walked every time a match starts, the replay list opens, an unstarted match is cleaned up or an account is deleted. Nobody notices at today's size, but it gets slower with every game played. Once built, those links are indexed, and a check fails if a new one arrives without an index.

## Why
I measured this on a throwaway `postgres:16` with every migration (0001–0055) applied, listing the foreign keys whose columns lead no index. 19 of 86 have none, including:
- `tickets(match_id) → matches` (on delete set null).
  - `matches_mode_of` reads it (`crates/server/src/db/pg.rs:3384`, `where t.match_id = m.id`) at every match start and rebuild (`actor/registry.rs:226`, `:325`). It also runs for each row of the replay list (`api/replays.rs:418`), each game record (`api/game_records.rs:127`), each reaped result (`api/results.rs:744`) and each rematch (`api/rematch.rs:423`).
  - Every `delete from public.matches` walks it.
  - Nothing ever deletes old tickets; only an account deletion's cascade removes a player's own. So the table grows with every queue.
- `profiles(current_match_id) → matches`: walked by every match delete and by the open-row reaper's join (`pg.rs:6275-6284`).
- `match_actions(player_id) → profiles` and `results(winner_profile_id) → profiles` (on delete set null): an account deletion (migration 0012) sets them to null by scanning every logged action and every result.
- `duos_rooms(host)`, `duos_rooms(guest)`, `replay_shares(sharer)` and `invite_codes(created_by)`, all to profiles: walked by every account deletion.
- `trios(profile_id, deckN_id) → decks`, three keys: walked when a deck is deleted.
- The other 8 point at the catalog tables (`cards`, `cosmetics`), which the server never deletes from (only test probes do).

`crates/server/tests/sql/01_schema_invariants.sql` CHECK 16 asserts the matchmaking tables' indexes by name, but nothing asserts that a foreign key is indexed.

## Proposal
- Add migration `0056_foreign_key_indexes.sql` with `create index if not exists` for the 11 keys above that don't point at a catalog table, partial (`where … is not null`) on the nullable ones. Register it in `crates/server/src/db/migrate.rs`, in `tests/sql/run.sh`'s batch list and in `tests/store/migrations_pinned.rs`.
- Add a check to `01_schema_invariants.sql`: every foreign key in `public` that doesn't reference a named catalog table (`cards`, `cosmetics`) has an index whose leading columns are the key's columns. The check fails naming the key.
- The check counts an index only if it has no predicate, or only the key's own `is not null`. My count above accepted any index, so this stricter check also flags `tickets(profile_id)`, whose only index is partial (`tickets_profile_queued_key`, `where status = 'queued'`) and so can't serve an account deletion's cascade. The migration indexes it too, along with any other key the stricter check finds.
- Add a line to `crates/server/README.md`'s migration notes.

## Where it lands
- `crates/server/migrations/0056_foreign_key_indexes.sql`, `crates/server/src/db/migrate.rs`
- `crates/server/tests/sql/run.sh`, `crates/server/tests/sql/01_schema_invariants.sql`, `crates/server/tests/store/migrations_pinned.rs`
- `crates/server/README.md`. SPEC §9.1's schema, with no rule change.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `sh crates/server/tests/sql/run.sh` passes, and its new check fails when one of the new indexes is dropped (shown in the pull request).
- [ ] After the migrations, no foreign key lacks a leading index except those into `cards` and `cosmetics`.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-server` (pinned migration checksums included) and `sh crates/server/tests/db/run.sh` pass.
- [ ] The migration only adds indexes and changes no data.

## Size and risks
Small to medium: one migration, one check and three registrations. CLAUDE.md rule 11 rates a migration hard. Each migration runs in one transaction, so the indexes are built without `concurrently`, which briefly blocks writes to each table while its index builds. At today's sizes that is a moment, but the deploy is best kept away from peak play.

--   * into public.profiles, walked by every account deletion (0012):
--     match_actions.player_id, results.winner_profile_id,
--     invite_codes.created_by, duos_rooms.host and guest, replay_shares.sharer,
--     and four whose only leading index is partial on another predicate, so it

--     chat_messages.to_profile (chat_messages_unread_idx) and duos_matches.a1

--   * into public.decks, walked by every deck delete: trios' three slot keys,

--     which a profile's few trios keep cheap; they get their own so that
--     tests/sql/01_schema_invariants.sql CHECK 19 holds every key alike.

-- An index on a nullable key is partial on `is not null`: a lookup by the key
-- never matches a null, so the rows it leaves out are never looked for. The
-- keys into the catalog (public.cards, public.cosmetics) stay as they are: the
-- server never deletes a catalog row.
--
-- Only indexes, no data. Each is built in this file's transaction, so without
-- `concurrently`, holding writes to its table while it builds.
--
-- Apply order: 0001 (profiles, invite_codes) -> 0004 (matches, tickets,
-- match_actions, results) -> 0007 (trios) -> ... -> 0038 (challenges,
-- chat_messages, replay_shares) -> 0039 (duos_rooms, duos_matches) -> ... ->
-- 0055 -> 0056 (this file).

  on public.tickets (match_id) where match_id is not null;
create index if not exists profiles_current_match_id_idx
  on public.profiles (current_match_id) where current_match_id is not null;

-- Into public.profiles.

  on public.match_actions (player_id) where player_id is not null;
create index if not exists results_winner_profile_id_idx
  on public.results (winner_profile_id) where winner_profile_id is not null;
create index if not exists invite_codes_created_by_idx
  on public.invite_codes (created_by) where created_by is not null;
create index if not exists duos_rooms_host_idx on public.duos_rooms (host);
create index if not exists duos_rooms_guest_idx
  on public.duos_rooms (guest) where guest is not null;
create index if not exists replay_shares_sharer_idx on public.replay_shares (sharer);
create index if not exists tickets_profile_id_idx on public.tickets (profile_id);
create index if not exists challenges_from_idx on public.challenges (from_profile);
create index if not exists chat_messages_to_idx on public.chat_messages (to_profile);
create index if not exists duos_matches_a1_idx

create index if not exists duos_matches_a2_idx
  on public.duos_matches (a2) where a2 is not null;

-- Into public.decks.

\echo '=== CHECK 19: every foreign key in public, but those into the catalog, has an index that leads with its columns ==='
-- A delete of a referenced row (an account, a match, a deck) looks up the rows that point at it
-- by the key's columns, as the server's reads by such a link do, and with no index leading with
-- those columns each such lookup reads the whole table (#1800, migration 0056). An index counts
-- only if it is a valid btree whose leading key columns are the foreign key's, in any order, and
-- it is whole or partial on nothing but one of the key's own columns `is not null`: a lookup by
-- the key never matches a null, so that predicate never hides a row it needs, while any other one
-- (tickets_profile_queued_key's `status = 'queued'`) does. The keys into the catalog tables
-- (`cards`, `cosmetics`) are exempt: the server never deletes a catalog row.
create temp view check19_foreign_keys as
select c.conrelid::regclass::text as tbl,
       c.conname,
       (select string_agg(a.attname, ', ' order by k.ord)
          from unnest(c.conkey) with ordinality k(attnum, ord)
          join pg_attribute a on a.attrelid = c.conrelid and a.attnum = k.attnum) as cols,
       c.confrelid::regclass::text as refs,
       exists (
         select 1
           from pg_index x
           join pg_class ic on ic.oid = x.indexrelid
           join pg_am am on am.oid = ic.relam
          where x.indrelid = c.conrelid
            and x.indisvalid
            and am.amname = 'btree'
            and x.indnkeyatts >= cardinality(c.conkey)
            and (select array_agg(k order by k)
                   from unnest((x.indkey::int2[])[0:cardinality(c.conkey) - 1]) k)
                = (select array_agg(k order by k) from unnest(c.conkey) k)
            and (x.indpred is null
                 or pg_get_expr(x.indpred, x.indrelid) in (
                      select format('(%s IS NOT NULL)', quote_ident(a.attname))
                        from pg_attribute a
                       where a.attrelid = c.conrelid and a.attnum = any (c.conkey)))) as indexed
  from pg_constraint c
  join pg_namespace n on n.oid = c.connamespace
 where c.contype = 'f'
   and n.nspname = 'public'
   and c.confrelid <> all (array['public.cards'::regclass, 'public.cosmetics'::regclass]);
select tbl, conname, cols, refs from check19_foreign_keys where not indexed order by 1, 2;
do $$
declare
  total     int;
  offenders text;
begin
  select count(*),
         string_agg(format('%s.%s (%s) -> %s', tbl, conname, cols, refs), '; ' order by tbl, conname)
           filter (where not indexed)
    into total, offenders
    from check19_foreign_keys;
  if total = 0 then
    raise exception 'FAIL (CHECK 19): no foreign key in public outside the catalog — the migrations did not apply';
  end if;
  if offenders is not null then
    raise exception
      'FAIL (CHECK 19): foreign key(s) with no index leading with their columns: % — add one in a new migration',
      offenders;
  end if;
  raise notice 'OK (CHECK 19): all % foreign keys in public outside the catalog have an index leading with their columns',
    total;
end $$;
```
````
